title: Varna 12. The Account of the Disappearance of Sri Jagadisha Pandita
html:
Invocation of Jagadisha; Raghunatha Acharya settles in Malipara and spreads devotion to Hari, Kamalakanta Dasa of Durgapur makes bhakti manifest in his own country, and Jagadisha's disciples establish sankirtana; a daughter, Rasamanjari, and a son, Ramabhadra, are born to Jagadisha and Duhkhini; Jagadisha seeks a match for his daughter with Gopala-vallabha, the son of Madhava Acharya and of Gangadevi, Nityananda's daughter, at Jirat; Madhava Acharya consults Gangadevi and comes to Yashoda; the weddings of the daughter and the son; Jagadisha infuses his power into his son Ramabhadra; Jagadisha's disappearance on the bright third tithi of the month of Pausha and his departure to Vrindavana; in Vraja he is Kalavati-jiu; an appeal to Jagadisha's disciples and the fruit of hearing; a list of the contents of the twelve varnas; the author's self-abasement and a shloka; a song of prayer to Gauranga; glorification of Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita, Srinivasa, Gadadhara and the six Gosvamis; entreaty to the devotees and to Bhagavatananda; the author's signature; the closing shloka and the date of the manuscript

The twelfth varna

1Glory, glory to Jagadisha, the ocean of mercy!
Mercifully deliver me, a sinner.

2Thus Raghunatha Acharya Mahashaya,
having received initiation and instruction, went to his own home.

3His dwelling was in the village of Malipara;
there he established devotion to Hari.1

4Sri Kamalakanta Dasa, a resident of Durgapur,
going to his own country, made bhakti manifest [there].2

5Thus the disciples of Sri Jagadisha
all established the sankirtana of Hari.

6Meanwhile Prabhu Jagadisha, remaining in Yashoda,
delivered many souls by giving them devotion to Krishna.

7Thus many people became devotees of Krishna;
by the power of kirtana the minds of all were purified.

8At this the Pandita was filled with joy
and lived in his own home, happy at heart.

9After some time, by the mercy of Mahaprabhu,
one daughter and one son were born to the Pandita.3

10The daughter was given the name Sri Rasamanjari,
and the son received the name Sri Ramabhadra.

11Having obtained a daughter and a son, Duhkhini, joyful at heart,
serves the feet of Gauranga with firm devotion.

12After some time their daughter reached the age for marriage,
and Prabhu began to ponder over her wedding.4

13As he pondered and pondered, he remembered
that at the shripat of Jirat dwells Ganga Gosvami.5

14She is the daughter of Prabhu Nityananda;
throughout the three worlds she is highly honoured.

15Her husband is Sri Madhava Acharya Mahashaya,
noble in every respect, both in worldly dealings and in the highest goal.

16His son is named Gopala-vallabha;
"To him I shall give my daughter," [Jagadisha] decided.6

17Having settled this in his mind, the Thakura Pandita
quickly sent a brahmana to Jirat.

18That brahmana, going to Sri Madhava Acharya,
tells him in detail what is in the Pandita's mind.

19Hearing this, Sri Madhava Acharya Mahashaya,
with joy in his heart, reflects:

20"To marry my son to Jagadisha's daughter —
this I have firmly decided."

21Having reflected thus, he entered the inner apartments
and told Sri Gangadevi all that had happened:

22"Jagadisha Pandita is a mahanta of great mind;
he has a daughter endowed with every good quality.

23For the sake of her marriage with my son
he has sent a brahmana to me.

24Tell me what your wish is:
I want to send the brahmana back quickly."

25Hearing this, Gangadevi said to him:
"Whatever your wish is, to that I give my consent.

26But if you yourself ask what is in my mind —
I know that Jagadisha is a venerable mahanta.

27If he gives his daughter to my son,
that is what should be done — such is my decision."

28Hearing [this], Sri Madhava Acharya was pleased
and, taking that brahmana with him, came to Yashoda.

29Learning [of this], Jagadisha went out to meet him and received him,
and seated him on a wonderful seat.

30The two sat and conversed for some time about the Lord;
then Jagadisha speaks these words to him:

31"Your son Gopivallabha Mahashaya —
to him I shall give my daughter: such is my decision.

32Tell me what should be done about it —
this is my request to you."

33Hearing this, Sri Madhava Acharya says to him:
"I shall tell you what is in my mind:

34to marry my son to your daughter —
such is my decision."

35Having spoken thus, the two then fixed the auspicious hour,
and on an auspicious day the Pandita gave his daughter in marriage.

36Some time after that the Pandita Thakura
with great joy arranged his son's wedding.

37Having married his daughter and his son, the Thakura Pandita
joyfully serves Jagannatha.

38Thus Jagadisha follows the duties of a householder
and, giving the name of Hari, delivers many souls.

39Into his own son Ramabhadra he infused his power (shakti),
and he, giving bhakti, delivered many souls.

40If all that were described, the book would become very long;
for this reason I have written down [only] selected parts of it.7

41I bow to his lotus feet —
may there be no offence on my part in this.

42Thus Sri Jagadisha, having delivered the souls,
disappeared, meditating on the feet of Gaura.8

43In the month of Pausha, in the bright fortnight, on the day of the third tithi,
he disappeared and went to Vrindavana.

44Who has the power to describe the life of Jagadisha,
who is famed in Vraja under the name Kalavati-jiu?9

45To assist in the lilas of Gauranga,
he descended in a male form in the house of a brahmana.

46Having accomplished his task, he went again to Vrindavana;
a small part of his lilas is described in this book.

47To all who have taken shelter of Prabhu Jagadisha
I make this request:

48hear this life of Jagadisha
and with devotion worship the feet of Jagadisha.

49One to whom Jagadisha shows compassion
attains Vrindavana without difficulty.

50The lilas of Prabhu Jagadisha are endless and boundless:
I have no power to describe them in full.

51Prabhu Bhagavatananda gave the order in a dream;
by his order this description in the form of a sutra came about.10

52Merely by hearing this, all sins are destroyed,
and residence in the abode of Vrindavana is attained without difficulty.

53Now I shall tell of Jagadisha's lilas in order:
in the first varna — the mangalacharana.11

54In the second varna — Prabhu's birth and annaprashana,
in the third varna — the description of the upanayana.

55In the fourth varna — how Prabhu taught the shastras
and refuted the wrong understanding of a brahmana who held that [God] is formless.

56In the fifth varna — the description of Prabhu's wedding,
and there too the birth of Mahesha Pandita is recorded.

57In the sixth — the disappearance of Prabhu's father and mother;
Prabhu performed the shraddha and other rites by the injunctions of the shastras.

58Leaving the eastern country, the brahmana went to Navadvipa
and settled there near the Ganga.

59In the seventh — the meeting with Mahaprabhu:
Mahaprabhu ate the offering for Vishnu.12

60In the eighth Jagadisha Pandita Mahashaya
went to Niladri by the Lord's order.

61Bringing from there the body of Jagannatha,
he himself manifested [His] service in Yashoda.13

62In the ninth — Gauranga's coming to Yashoda:
the Lord, having asked for it Himself, ate payasa.

63Prabhu Nityananda asked for a meal of whatever He wished,
and the Pandita fed [Him] according to [His] wish.

64In the tenth — the account of the installation of Gaura-Gopala
and of the Lord's coming again to the Pandita's house.

65In the eleventh Mahaprabhu, filled with joy,
went to Sri Kshetra, taking the Pandita with Him.

66There too the birth of Raghunatha Acharya is described,
and how Jagadisha gave him initiation and instruction.

67A certain worthy man named Kamalakanta Dasa
took shelter of Jagadisha's feet.

68In the twelfth — Sri Jagadisha, having performed various lilas
and delivered many fallen souls, disappeared.

69In twelve varnas the book has been completed:
I have described [everything] only briefly, in the form of a sutra.

70Jagadisha's lilas are filled with millions of oceans of nectar;
fortunate is he who relishes them.

71I am an insignificant soul, a low sinner:
O Vaishnava Thakura, forgive [my] offences.

72I am extremely dull-witted, greedy for sense objects;
I wander about ever maddened, under the sway of maya.

73I do not know good from bad — I am a fool;
for my own purification I offer this praise.

74Out of compassion Mahaprabhu descended
and delivered the greatest of sinners.

75By Gauranga's mercy His sadhus appeared,
and they delivered a multitude of souls.

76I am the most foolish of the low, and moreover I do not know bhajana:
how should I know how to sing the Lord's praise?

77I have no discernment of good and bad, my mind is not pure:
I have no power to sing the Lord's praise.

78As the Lord's dear devotees have described [it],
following that, I offer a little praise.

Tatha hi:

79"I am not skilled, not virtuous, and no knower of the shastras;
I have no good qualities, I am not wise and not versed in dharma.
Me, incapable of anything, fallen, afflicted — O Lord, O Friend, alas, alas! —
O Delight of Shachi's heart, protect, protect!"14

80Have mercy, Gorachand, ocean of compassion!
I am exceedingly sinful, and You are the deliverer of the fallen,
the friend of the humble, the destitute and those who have nothing.15

81I am a sinner with evil desires, my mind is unsteady,
day and night it is agitated among sense objects.
Devoid of bhakti, utterly wretched, devoid of bhajana and sadhana —
therefore my heart is in great fear.

82Never have I been skilled, there is no virtue in me,
and moreover I am not versed in the shastras.
Ever immersed in evil objects, never have I been wise,
nor am I versed in dharma.

83In the three worlds there is no one as sinful as I —
therefore all disregard [me].
Thinking of this, my heart ever trembles and quakes:
in no way do I see protection [for myself].

84Consider and see: there is no end to my sins,
my mind is skilled in evil deeds.
You bear the name of the Merciful One, Prabhu, beautiful Gauranga —
this time protect, protect me!

85Descending to the earth, You delivered many sinners —
but in that, I think, there is no glory [for You].
If, however, You, Prabhu, can deliver me, a low sinner,
then [Your] glory will remain in the three worlds.

86Having delivered many sinners, You did not look at me —
because of this there is fear in my mind:
You bear the name Patita-pavana, Prabhu, abode of virtues —
lest a stain fall on [that] name!

87I am an insignificant, wretched soul; absorbed in sense objects,
I did not worship Your feet.
But You, Prabhu, are an ocean of mercy, the friend of low people:
this word is proclaimed everywhere.

88You are the Sustainer of countless universes, You are the father of all,
all living beings are Your children.
If by ill fate a son goes away elsewhere,
the father never abandons him.

89All the living beings in the universe You delivered in various ways,
no one's ill fate remained:
by the power of Your compassion they all easily
crossed the ocean of Your maya.

90Listen, Prabhu Gaurahari, this I pray:
my birth is within [that same] universe.
If, then, I remain lying [in it], suffering the torments of the three miseries,
it must be according to [my] past karma.

91Descending in the Kali-yuga, You made a vow:
"I shall deliver the greatest of sinners."
In my mind there is this sorrow: because of me, it seems,
Your vow has not been kept.

92Or else at the time of [Your] descent You made such a vow:
"All living beings except me
I shall easily deliver, I shall give [them] krishna-prema and bhakti" —
for this reason I have been left out.

93But in this there is no fault [of Yours]; listen, merciful Gaura,
I pray [to You] again and again:
I have described this book — whatever faults have occurred in it,
forgive me for them.16

94Not knowing good from bad, I describe the lilas of Your branch,
being an exceedingly insignificant soul.
Mercifully bring it about
that the devotees accept this book.17

95Whatever may fall to my lot — I give no thought to that at all,
in my mind there is only one desire:
the book came about with great labour by the command of Bhagavata[nanda] —
may the devotees accept it.18

96Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to blessed Nityananda!
Glory, glory to Sri Advaitachandra!
Glory to Srinivasa, glory to Gadadhara, full of prema!
Glory, glory to the host of Gaura's devotees!19

97Glory to Rupa and Sanatana, whose life's treasure is Gaura!
Glory, glory to Bhatta Raghunatha!
Glory to Sri Jiva Gosani — there is no one as merciful as he:
he makes the fallen his own.

98Glory to Sri Gopala Bhatta, full of supreme compassion,
whose life is Sri Radharamana,
whose disciple Srinivasa, bringing the books to light,
saved the souls by the gift of bhakti.

99Glory to Raghunatha Dasa, Gauranga's dear servant,
ever intoxicated with singing Gaura's virtues,
from whom Sri Rupa Gosvami and others, day and night, without cease,
hear of Gaura's virtues.

100The countless mahantas, whose life's treasure
is Shachi's darling Gaurahari —
placing their holy feet upon my head,
I humbly make only this entreaty:

101may all their devotees, with joy,
accept this book.
Then the life of Jagadisha will spread everywhere:
whoever hears [it] will gain benefit.

102I am a person devoid of intelligence: this book, this description,
could never have come about from me.
If, then, the description has come about and I have put the letters together —
[it is] by the order of Prabhu Bhagavata[nanda].

103What that Prabhu said, that I wrote in the book;
it was completed by his wish.
If now the devotees accept the book,
then [my] labour will be fruitful.

104Devotees of Gaura, oceans of mercy, out of compassion
all of you place your feet upon my head.
Then, easily, by the power of the mercy of you all,
I shall cross this ocean of worldly existence.

105Prabhu Bhagavatananda, root of the world's joy,
free [me] from the fear of worldly existence.
Fallen into the ocean of existence, I call [to you] again and again:
this time save [me].

106Descending to the earth by Gauranga's order,
you delivered many sinners.
To so low a person as I you appeared in a dream —
shall I ever again obtain [your] darshana?

107As the order was [given] then, so the book was composed
by the humble and wretched Ananda Dasa.
I ask for nothing more: [let me] ever sing Gaura's virtues —
fulfil this desire.20

Thus in the Charitra-vijaya of Sri Jagadisha Pandita ends the twelfth varna, called "The Account of the Disappearance of Sri Jagadisha Pandita".21

108One who constantly hears with devotion the narrations about Gaura's devotees
becomes dear to Gaurachandra — of this there is no doubt.22

The Shaka year 1737.23

Notes

  1. Malipara (মালীপাড়া, mālīpāḍā) — the village where Raghunatha Acharya settled, the son of Bhagavan Acharya Khanja and a disciple of Jagadisha (varna 11).
  2. Kamalakanta Dasa of Durgapur — a disciple of Jagadisha (varna 11, note 8). «দেশে গিয়া» (deśe giyā) — "going to [his own] country".
  3. Cf. varna 9, 104–106: there Jagadisha's three earlier sons, at his own request, left their bodies and merged into the body of Gauranga. Here a daughter, Rasamanjari, and a son, Ramabhadra, are born (10).
  4. «কতদিনে দুহিকার কন্যা কাল হৈল» (katadine duhikāra kanyā-kāla haila) — the reading «দুহিকার» is unclear; taken as «দুঁহাকার» (duṅhākāra), "of the two of them" (Jagadisha and Duhkhini); «কন্যা কাল» — "the maiden's time", the age for marriage.
  5. Shripat (শ্রীপাট, śrīpāṭa) — the holy residence of a Vaishnava. Jirat (জিরাট, jirāṭa) — the shripat of Ganga, Nityananda's daughter; "Ganga Gosvami" (গঙ্গাগোস্বামী, gaṅgā-gosvāmī) is as in the text; in 21 and 25 she is called Gangadevi. Her husband Madhava Acharya (15) is a disciple and son-in-law of Nityananda.
  6. The son of Madhava Acharya and Gangadevi is named in the text in two ways: «গোপাল বল্লভ» (gopāla ballabha, Gopala-vallabha, 16) and «গোপীবল্লভ» (gopīballabha, Gopivallabha, 31); translated as in the text.
  7. «এ কারণে লিখিলুঁ বি·শষ তাহার» (e kāraṇe likhiluṅ biśeṣa tāhāra) — one letter is damaged in the edition; taken as «বিশেষ» (biśeṣa), "particular, selected". Possibly «না» (nā) has dropped out: "for this reason I have not written it down in detail" (cf. varna 11, 101).
  8. «অন্তর্দ্ধান» (antardhāna) — "disappearance": so Vaishnavas call the departure of the Lord's associate from the manifest lila. According to the author, Jagadisha went to Vrindavana (43, 46). In the second line of 43 the rhyme is imperfect (দিন / বৃন্দাবনে).
  9. «জীউ» (jīu) — the respectful "-ji". According to GGD 143, Jagadisha Pandita in Krishna-lila is Chandrahasa, a dancer of Vraja; Kalavati in GGD 188 is one of the sakhis who sang Vishakha's songs, and she is identified there with another associate. The identification of Jagadisha with Kalavati is the author's; cf. 45: "descended in a male form".
  10. «সূত্র বর্ণন» (sūtra varṇana) — "a description in the form of a sutra", i.e. briefly, only the essentials (cf. 69). On Bhagavatananda's order in a dream — varna 11, 104–106.
  11. In 53–68 the author lists the contents of the twelve varnas; cf. their colophons. In 54 «জন্মান্ন প্রাশন» (janmānna prāśana) — "birth and annaprashana".
  12. Cf. varna 7 and varna 6, note 9: in the CB and CC the episode of the offering for Vishnu on Ekadashi is connected with the Jagadisha of the pair "Jagadisha and Hiranya".
  13. Niladri — Puri. "Body" (কলেবর, kalevara) — the body of the Deity Jagannatha, brought by Jagadisha (varna 8, note 7).
  14. The source of the shloka has not been established. «সর্বাক্ষমং পতিত মার্ত্তম» is taken as sarvākṣamaṁ patitam ārtam. Stanza 82 paraphrases the first half of the shloka.
  15. After this stanza the edition has «ধ্রু» (dhru, "dhruva") — the refrain of the song; stanzas 81–107 are tripadi. «কৃপাকর» (kṛpākara) is taken as «কৃপা কর» (kṛpā kara), "have mercy"; Gorachand (গোরাচান্দ, gorācānda) — Gaurachandra.
  16. In the edition the punctuation in 93 is shifted («…বারে বারে ॥» / «…আমারে।»); the stanza is arranged by rhyme (বারে বারে / আমারে).
  17. «তব শাখা লীলা» (taba śākhā līlā) — "the lilas of Your branch": Jagadisha is a branch of the tree of Sri Chaitanya; in the CC Jagadisha Pandita is named among the branches of Nityananda (Adi 11).
  18. «ভাগবত» (bhāgavata, 95, 102) — Bhagavatananda, who commanded the author in a dream to write the book (cf. 51, 105–106; varna 11, note 18).
  19. Srinivasa (শ্রীনিবাস, śrīnivāsa) in 96 is Srivasa Pandita (in GGD 12, "Srinivasa Pandita"), named alongside Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita and Gadadhara; in 98 — Srinivasa Acharya, the disciple of Gopala Bhatta. Bhatta Raghunatha — Raghunatha Bhatta Gosvami; Gosani — Gosvami; Sri Radharamana — the Deity of Gopala Bhatta in Vrindavana.
  20. The author's signature is a variant of the formula.
  21. Before the colophon the edition has «পুষ্পিকাঃ» (puṣpikāḥ, "colophon"), apparently an editor's label. In the colophon «অন্তর্দ্ধান কথনং» (antardhāna kathanaṁ) — "the account of the disappearance".
  22. The closing shloka; the source has not been established.
  23. «শকাব্দাঃ — ১৭৩৭» (śakābdāḥ 1737) — the date of the manuscript on which the edition is based; the year 1737 of the Shaka era corresponds to 1815/1816 CE (the month is not given).
